clarification_questions.question: What exactly has to be measured - which component or property, and over what concentration or value range?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The target decides whether MIR, Raman or NIR can see it at all.

clarification_questions.question: Is the liquid clear, turbid or opaque, and does it contain particles, colour or gas bubbles?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: The optical regime decides between transmission, transflection, reflection and ATR.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy and response time are required, and which reference method will be used to verify the results?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: These criteria set the go/no-go basis and can rule methods in or out.

clarification_questions.question: What are the process conditions at the measurement point (temperature, pressure, flow, cleaning), and how is the probe installed (port, line size, distance to the instrument)?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: They constrain the probe, the fiber type and the length of the link.

clarification_questions.question: Is the liquid water-based, and does it contain a fluorescent species?
clarification_questions.why_it_matters: Water content and fluorescence background shift the choice between MIR, Raman and fluorescence.

recommendations.rationale: MIR ATR works on liquids in contact with the crystal, and mid-IR is described as one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis, so it is the first method to test. The nominal mid-IR range is 4000-400 cm-1; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe actually selected.
recommendations.conditions: Requires the liquid to wet and make tight contact with the ATR crystal.

citations.quote: Vibrational spectroscopy in the mid-IR range (4000-400 cm-1) is one of the most informative methods of chemical analysis.
ATR fiber probes (Fig.1) enable the analysis of liquids and solid elastic samples
Probe-based analysis is gaining widespread use in online analysis, such as in-line, in-process (chemical, biotechnological, natural) environments

recommendations.rationale: Raman carries complementary vibrational information to mid-IR and tolerates water, so it is worth testing on the same liquid. The Raman shift (cm-1) is stated separately from the laser excitation wavelength (nm), and the usable range depends on the probe and spectrometer selected.

citations.quote: This property makes mid-IR and Raman spectra complementary, that is, they complement each other.
Raman is particularly well-suited for aqueous environments, as it exhibits low absorbance for water molecules compared to infrared methods.
The Raman shift is used as the horizontal (spectral) axis in Raman spectroscopy

recommendations.rationale: NIR transmission or transflection is preferred for transparent or semi-transparent liquids and is the most common online method with fiber probes. It applies only if the liquid turns out clear; a turbid or opaque liquid would need a reflection geometry instead.
recommendations.conditions: Applies only if the liquid is transparent or semi-transparent at the measurement point.

citations.quote: Transmission is the preferred method for transparent or semi-transparent liquids, such as skim milk, whey, or permeate.
Near-IR vibrational spectroscopy (NIR) is the most common online analysis method performed using fiber optic probes.
it fails when the milk becomes too "thick" or fat-rich, as the light cannot penetrate the sample.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: Single-method fiber probes at the process point first: an ATR immersion probe (MIR), a Raman contact probe, or a transmission/transflexion probe for a clear liquid. A combined probe is a later hypothesis only.
measurement_concept.location: In-line, at a point in the customer's line or vessel that is still to be named.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: The fiber family follows the method: MIR light is not carried by silica fibers. No supplied source states an achievable length for an in-line MIR link, so the link length is an open question for AFS.

solution_options.ease_of_use: two spectrometers, combined probe, more setup
solution_options.performance_fit: complementary MIR and Raman information per sample
solution_options.cost_drivers: two spectrometers, combined probe, fusion software, reference data
solution_options.fusion_note: Fusion level: one model per method first, then a joined or score-level model with block scaling, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. Both techniques must look at the same small area of the liquid and the two data streams must be aligned to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.

citations.quote: It is crucial that the spectral information obtained by different methods-Mid-IR, NIR, Raman, and fluorescence spectra-is collected from the same small, even pinpoint, area of the sample.
Ultimately, the measurement data must be normalized to a common time step.
If the variables have different units of measurement, the data should be normalized in some way, for example, using an autoscaling algorithm.
This property makes mid-IR and Raman spectra complementary, that is, they complement each other.
compare with the best single method.

proposal.what_would_change_it: A named target with its range, the liquid's optical regime and the required accuracy would decide the method: a clear, low-optical-density liquid would move the choice to NIR transmission (M3), while an aqueous sample with a strong fluorescence background would favour Raman or the combined probe (O3).
proposal.next_step: Answer the clarification questions, then run a single-method comparison on representative samples of the liquid before any in-line installation.

solution_options.fusion_note: Fusion level: one model per method first, then a joined or score-level model with block scaling, because variables from different methods are not equivalent. Both techniques must look at the same small area of the liquid and the two data streams must be aligned to a common time step. Each method keeps its own calibration and diagnostics, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.
